title: France – Architectural and related services – Marché de maîtrise d'oeuvre relative au projet de réhabilitation de l'église Saint-Etienne à Cernay
description: Mission de base de maîtrise d'oeuvre (domaine opérations de réhabilitation de bâtiment patrimonial), comportant : avant-projet sommaire (APS), avant-projet définitif (APD), études de projet (PRO) incluant l'établissement des dossiers de consultation des entreprises, assistance au maître d'ouvrage pour la passation des contrats de travaux (ACT), direction de l'exécution des contrats de travaux (DET), assistance lors des opérations de réception et pendant la période de garantie de parfait achèvement (AOR). Missions complémentaires : diagnostic du bâtiment (DIA) ; relevés-vérifications complémentaires de l'église et des éléments liturgiques (plans partiels et nuages de points fournis) ; étude comparative de deux scénarios (réhabilitation du choeur) ; étude d'approvisionnement énergétique (chauffage, électricité...) ; coordination des systèmes de sécurité incendie (CSSI) ; assistance à l'établissement des dossiers de subvention ; études d'exécution et synthèse (EXE-SYN) ; ordonnancement, pilotage et coordination du chantier (OPC) ; assistance à l'information des usagers. Le marché est décomposé en une tranche ferme et deux tranches optionnelles. Tranche ferme : APS et APD, DIA, relevés-vérifications complémentaires, étude comparative de deux scénarios, étude d'approvisionnement énergétique, CSSI, assistance à l'établissement des dossiers de subvention ; elle se conclut par la fixation du coût prévisionnel des travaux et du forfait définitif de rémunération. Tranche optionnelle 1 : PRO, ACT, EXE-SYN. Tranche optionnelle 2 : DET, AOR, OPC, assistance à l'information des usagers.

title: Q301--Biodesix, Inc. (621 II) (PENDING PROPOSAL)
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. Enter Nationwide if currently/recently providing nationwide (i.e. domestic delivery) coverage. Proposed Coverage: Offerors may propose to provide service to individual states or nationwide. Respond to each question below regarding proposed coverage. For each choice selected, you must also check the box to verify your submission of the requested supporting documentation. title: Q702--Santa Maria IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Santa Maria, CA OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for the Santa Maria Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 31-months. VHA authorized a 28,656 net usable square foot (NUSF) outpatient clinic (OPC) lease project in Santa Maria, California. The project will support the parent facility, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System. The new OPC will replace the existing clinic in Santa Maria, which currently contains 28,612 NUSF. The new clinic will be able to accommodate future workload, provide ample parking (200 spaces), and will adequately support all services in a modern, efficient space. The new clinic will provide all the services offered at the existing clinic, including Primary Care, Mental Health, Audiology, Eye Clinic, Dental, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Pathology and Blood Draw, Logistics, Telehealth, Business Office, Community Engagement and Reintegration, and Women's Health. This new facility is essential to accommodate the current demand of 6,634 Unique Santa Maria Veterans and the future potential demand of 7,500 Santa Maria catchment Enrollees The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 30 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 30 November 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to both Katherine.Johnson6@va.gov and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for proposals. P.O.C: Katherine.Johnson@va.gov, Contract Specialist and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

(PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA) Primary Objective Engineer comprehensive design packages to repair, upgrade, and interconnect deteriorated electrical switching infrastructure Primary by Facility & Component ESS B18 (Switching Station Upgrade) � Full replacement of legacy switchgear with FR3 fluid, air-insulated switchgear (per latest UFC 3-550-01) � Life-cycle cost and sustainability integration (UFC 1-200-02) � Thermal partition separating switchgear room from power generation bay � Dedicated HVAC system and air conditioning ductwork � Sized space heating units � High-efficiency interior LED lighting ESS B168 (Repair, Upgrade & Hardening) � Complete switchgear replacement mirroring ESS B168b using FR3 air-insulated switchgear (UFC 3-550-01) � Sustainable design practices (UFC 1-200-02) � Dedicated single HVAC unit and duct system � Interior/exterior high-efficiency LED flood/task lighting � Raised roof profile with comprehensive crack sealing/insulation � Foundation pillar repairs, crawl space waterproofing, and rainwater gutter system � Motorized roll-up door, cyber/physical cypher-locked access doors, and motorized loading dock ramp with widened sidewalk High-Voltage Redundancy Cables � Design 4-circuit bidirectional interconnect (8 cables total) connecting ESS B18 and ESS B168 � Baseline routing derived from 2025 Engineering Study � Mandatory underground routing preference across base footprint � Aerial routing permitted strictly as secondary exception where subsurface obstructions prevent underground installation Wireless SCADA & Grid Telemetry � Air Force long-term smart-grid wireless connectivity architecture � Cell-enabled control panels reporting directly to electric shop web interface without physical comm trunk lines � Relay-to-control panel comm wiring for ESS B18 and ESS B168 � Additional telemetry control panel integrated into ESS B4505 (sub-station to B18) to monitor sub-station power load profiles Key Technical Standards & Compliance Baseline UFC 3-550-01 Exterior Electrical Power Distribution Mandates modern FR3 biodegradable, fire-resistant fluid dielectric air-insulated switchgears, significantly mitigating environmental and thermal hazards. UFC 1-200-02 High Performance and Sustainable Building Requirements Governs energy efficiency, life-cycle cost effectiveness, indoor environmental quality, and durable materials integration. PDB / OTA Authority Prototype / Collaboration Framework Fosters early contractor involvement during Phase 1 design, mitigating unforeseen site and subsurface risk prior to Phase 2 construction commitment. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. title: Request for Information - Contract Writing System Recompete
description: Request for Information Contract Writing System Recompete 2099AC27N00004 RFI-DO-27-002 The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions that can support the U.S. Department of the Treasury requirements for a contract writing system as part of the Contract Writing System Recompete. The Government seeks information regarding vendors� technical capabilities, available products and services, hosting, system functionality, integration, and ability to satisfy the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors should review the entire Technical Exhibit and identify capabilities, limitations, and potential alternatives. This RFI is solely for market research and acquisition planning and is not a solicitation. This is an RFI for market research purposes, and not a solicitation. 1. SCOPE SUMMARY (See attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements) The Department of the Treasury is conducting market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing an enterprise contract writing system solution to support Treasury acquisition and procurement operations. Technical Exhibit 1 identifies anticipated functional, technical, operational, security, hosting, integration, and support requirements designated as Mandatory or Value Added. The Government may use information obtained through this RFI to refine requirements and determine an appropriate acquisition strategy for any future solicitation. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information from interested vendors regarding their capabilities and potential solutions for a Contract Writing System to support the Department of the Treasury's acquisition and contracting requirements. The incumbent contractor providing the Department's existing Contract Writing System is Unison Software, Inc. II. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for any resulting contract has not been finalized. Additional information regarding the period of performance, implementation schedule, and other acquisition details may be provided in a future solicitation, should one be issued. III. POTENTIAL INDUSTRY DAY / PRODUCT DEMONSTRATIONS The Government may elect to conduct an Industry Day and/or schedule individual vendor demonstrations as part of its market research efforts to better understand available commercial contract writing systems, products, solutions, services, and capabilities relevant to this RFI and the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors may be invited to demonstrate their proposed solutions, highlight key features and functionality, and discuss how their offerings could address the Government's operational and technical needs. Participation in any Industry Day or vendor demonstration will be voluntary and at the Government's sole discretion. Additional information regarding scheduling, format, and participation requirements will be provided if the Government determines that such an event would be beneficial. The Government is under no obligation to conduct an Industry Day or vendor demonstrations. Any such activities will be conducted solely for market research and informational purposes and will not constitute a formal evaluation of offers or quotations. Participation or nonparticipation will not guarantee or preclude consideration for, or award of, any future contract. IV. ADDITIONAL DETAILS NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. A request for more information, or a copy of the solicitation, will not be considered an affirmative response to this Request for Information. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Request for Information will NOT be accepted. Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC) will consider responses received no later than 10:00 AM ET, November 30, 2026, as submitted in writing to chad.gambrill@treasury.gov and paul.white2@treasury.gov. Please include �RFI: 2099AC27N00004, Contract Writing System Recompete- CG/PW� in the subject line. The Government is conducting market research to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions. Quotations and formal proposals will not be accepted at this time. The Government may, at its discretion, request clarification or additional technical information from responding vendors or conduct discussions associated with a potential Industry Day or vendor demonstration. Qualified contractors must provide the following: 1. The name and location of your company, contact information, and identify your business size and socioeconomic category. Please ensure contact information includes the name of the point of contact, email address, and telephone number should the Government have questions regarding individual responses. 2. The GSA contract or other vehicle your services are available through, including the schedule/GWAC number, NAICS Codes, and applicable SIN. 3. Capability Statement: Responding vendors shall provide a general capabilities statement describing their company, relevant experience, available contract writing system solutions, and technical capabilities. Responses should address the functional, technical, operational, hosting, integration, security, and support requirements identified in Technical Exhibit 1. 4. Technical Exhibit Response: Vendors are requested to complete the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. For each applicable requirement, indicate whether the proposed solution meets the requirement in the "Meets (Y/N)" column and provide explanatory information in the "Comments" column, as appropriate. For requirements not fully met, identify limitations, alternatives, or other approaches. Address both Mandatory and Value Added requirements. The following file extensions are not allowable and application materials/data submitted with these extensions cannot be considered: .bat, .cmd, .com, .exe, .pif, .rar, .scr, .vbs, .hta,, .cpl, and .zip files. Microsoft Office compatible documents are acceptable. Additional information regarding this RFI, including any potential Industry Day or vendor demonstrations, may be provided at the Government discretion. This notice does not restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. All firms responding to this notice are advised that their response is not a request that will be considered for contract award. All interested parties are required to respond to any resultant solicitation separately from their response to this notice, should one be issued.

title: Firefox
description: UPDATE: The purpose of Amendment 1 to DARPA-PA-26-137, the Firefox Program Solicitation (PS), is to update the deadlines for OPP submissions and presentations. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has developed a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals in humans. To expand this foundational technology and enable the development of revolutionary, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), DARPA's Firefox program is soliciting approaches to overcome key technological hurdles: 1) development of components enabling dynamic rastering/scanning of the incoming coherent optical signal to target multiple regions of interest and 2) development of new data processing architectures beyond the digital domain to handle the high data rates and computational burden inherent to scaling the amount of neural data recorded by the optical system. The ultimate goal of the Firefox program is to use these innovations to develop a 100-channel, non-invasive BCI with 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution.

Hormis pour le BET acoustique. title: 19WA8026Q0036 - Janitorial services at Embassy office building and Warehouse.
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The Embassy of the United States in Windhoek will launch the solicitation on the SAM.gov website when it is available. The U.S. Embassy in Windhoek hereby provides the following pre-solicitation notice in respect of the issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for: Janitorial/cleaning services at the U.S. Embassy Office building and General services warehouse in Windhoek, Namibia. The Contractor shall perform janitorial services in all designated spaces including, but not limited to halls, offices, restrooms, work areas, entrance ways, lobbies, storage areas, elevators, and stairways. The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The U.S. Government may award the contract, based on the initial offer, without any discussions. The resultant contract will be a fixed priced type of contract for its duration. The Government is planning a pre-quotation conference and the date for this conference will be in the solicitation. All contractors must be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) Database https://www.sam.gov prior to submitting an offer pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore, prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. This opportunity is subject to 52.229-12 - Tax on Certain Foreign Procurements (FEB 2021) Electronic Submission/Responses: This opportunity allows for electronic responses. Please submit your offer prior to the response date and time. Please ensure your email with your offer does not exceed 15 MB, if it does then you might have to send more than one email. Alternatively, offers may be submitted at the US Embassy offices at the following address: 38 Metje Street, Klein Windhoek, Windhoek, Namibia.

Alternatively, offers may be submitted at the U.S. Embassy offices at the following address: 38 Metje Street, Klein Windhoek, Windhoek, Namibia.

title: Saltash Guildhall Internal Works
description: Saltash Town Council is seeking tenders from suitably qualified contractors for internal remodelling works at the Guildhall, Lower Fore Street, Saltash. The project comprises refurbishment and adaptation works to support revised council operations and meeting functions, including: Manufacture and installation of bespoke horseshoe-shaped council chamber desking accommodating approximately 20 members/users. Supply and installation of audio visual equipment to support hybrid meetings, Microsoft Teams connectivity, microphones, displays, speakers and associated control systems. Installation of an assisted listening system. Electrical alterations and new power and data infrastructure within the First Floor Long Room. Electrical and data alterations within the Ground Floor Council Chamber. Electrical and data alterations within the Clerk's Office. Heating alterations including replacement radiators within the Council Chamber. Supply and installation of acoustic underlay and new carpet finishes within the First Floor Long Room. Associated commissioning, testing, certification, training and making good. The works will be undertaken within an occupied civic building and contractors must maintain safe operation of the premises throughout the contract period.

title: R799--Lake Baldwin EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought COR: Dustin Koonce
description: Lake Baldwin VA Clinic, FL EUL Request for Expressions of Interest 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY Orlando Healthcare System Veterans Integrated Service Network 08 (VISN 08) Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic - Orlando, FL Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the assets described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. An EUL is a long-term ground lease of underutilized VA-owned land or buildings to a non-federal entity (Developer). Under the EUL program, the Developer secures a long-term leasehold interest with VA for the subject property. This deal structure enables developers to finance, design, develop, renovate/construct, operate, and maintain improvements on VA property to directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program and sample EUL projects may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject assets in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigative activities to develop the selected assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic campus. VA is especially interested in development of supportive housing but will also consider other uses that benefit Veterans. The assets that may be redeveloped by a Developer include, but are not limited to, the following interconnected buildings (with current use in parentheses): Building 519 (Domiciliary) Building 519a (Dining / education space in the first floor courtyard) Building 520 (Domiciliary) Building 520a (Domiciliary reception / elevator space in Northwest corner of the interconnected buildings) Building 521 (Domiciliary) Building 522 (Domiciliary) Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. Lake Baldwin VA Clinic Background The Lake Baldwin VA Clinic in Orlando, Florida, traces its origins to a former U.S. Navy facility. In 1968, the Navy took over an Air Force hospital in the Lake Baldwin neighborhood, opening it as Naval Hospital Orlando. By 1995, the Navy closed Naval Hospital Orlando as part of broader base closures. The facility was then transferred to VA and rebranded as the Lake Baldwin VA Clinic. VA originally used the site as part of its outpatient and transitional care network, with some portions serving as labs, treatment spaces, and administrative offices. The 46-acre campus is located at 5201 Raymond Street, Orlando, FL 32803. The Lake Baldwin outpatient clinic offers urgent care, primary care, surgery, and specialty health services, including mental health care, laboratory services, vision care (optometry), pain management, prosthetics, physical therapy, nutrition services, homeless Veteran care, women Veteran care, and more. Sources Sought Response Requirements VA is seeking qualified developers who have a proven company track record of: Developing projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated assets. Financial wherewithal required to successfully develop the proposed use(s) with associated amenities (if applicable); and, Securing public and private financing for projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated assets. For SDVOSB/VOSB developers, VA is seeking to confirm the Respondent s ability to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. title: FWS - Pixley NWR Water Recirculation Design-Build
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes only solicitation. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, Pixley National Wildlife Refuge provides 755 acres of wetland habitat for migratory waterfowl and other water birds and relies on three deep groundwater wells for irrigation and flooding. This project will improve water reuse and reduce groundwater pumping demands, particularly during drought years. The contractor shall design and construct a water recirculation system consisting of approximately 1.2 miles of PVC pipeline connecting the wetlands� lowest topographical point to the existing pipeline farther east. The system shall include a pump at this low point to move water upslope for recirculation and critical irrigation. The contractor shall secure the pump station with a 12-foot-tall, gated chain-link enclosure topped with barbed wire. Excavated soil may be reused on refuge property, and restoration or seeding of disturbed ground will not be required. The construction magnitude is estimated to be between $700,000.00 to $750,000.00. title: Spain – Water-treatment chemicals – Suministro de reactivos para la potabilización del agua en las Estaciones de Tratamiento de Aguas Potables (ETAP) que gestiona Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA mediante sistema dinámico de adquisición
description: Las diferentes Estaciones de Tratamiento de Agua Potable ETAP gestionadas por Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA necesitan del suministro continuado de diferentes productos químicos a fin de garantizar el apropiado tratamiento y, por tanto, la salubridad del agua para poder cumplir con los parámetros exigidos por la normativa vigente para la potabilización del agua. Teniendo en cuenta la exhaustiva norma que regula la fabricación, transporte, descarga y dosificación de los productos empleados en la potabilización del agua de consumo humano y la necesidad permanente de suministro de tales productos, se hace necesaria la contratación de los mismos con empresas especializadas y que reúnan los requerimientos normativos exigidos para garantizar la salubridad del agua de consumo humano. La modalidad de contratación que se propone, a través de sistema dinámico de adquisición, nace de la necesidad de mejorar los tiempos de respuesta a determinadas necesidades de la organización.

description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. The Contractor must demonstrate technical capability conducting Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) bench-, pilot-, or full-scale efficacy evaluations targeting PFAS breakthrough and mass removal kinetics with preferred experience evaluating and optimizing existing pump-and-treat groundwater treatment plants (GWTPs) for PFAS removal across carbon be

description: ISBEE Set-Aside � Advanced Practice Provider Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner Services Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the HHS-adopted FAR Part 12, as supplemented by the attached solicitation documents. This announcement and its attachments constitute the solicitation. Quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal Advanced Practice Provider (APP) Physician Assistant (PA) and/or Nurse Practitioner (NP) healthcare services at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks a Contractor to provide qualified APP personnel sufficient to support two (2) full-time equivalent PA and/or NP positions providing outpatient primary care services at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic. Services include adult and pediatric primary care, chronic disease management, preventive and wellness services, acute outpatient care, authorized minor procedures, clinical documentation, referrals, care coordination, and quality-improvement activities. The Contractor shall furnish qualified licensed personnel, management, supervision, credentialing and privileging support, licensure and certification maintenance, professional liability insurance, staffing continuity, replacement personnel, and other Contractor-furnished resources necessary to perform the Performance Work Statement (PWS). This acquisition is set aside exclusively for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs). The assigned NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 million in average annual receipts. Quoters shall satisfy the applicable ISBEE eligibility and representation requirements and submit the completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form with their quotations. The anticipated award is a Firm-Fixed-Price, non-personal healthcare services purchase order using a Month-of-Service (MOS) pricing structure. One (1) MOS represents complete monthly performance of the required APP services, including qualified staffing equivalent to two (2) full-time PAs or NPs, scheduled outpatient clinic services, clinical documentation, care coordination, required training, and all other PWS requirements. The anticipated period of performance consists of a three (3)-month base period and three (3) option periods of three (3) months each, for a maximum potential period of performance of twelve (12) months. The anticipated base period is February 1, 2027, through April 30, 2027. Option-period dates will be specified in the resulting purchase order. Services will be performed at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic, 800 Hospital Drive, Rosebud, South Dakota 57570. Standard outpatient clinic hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding federal holidays, subject to the scheduling requirements identified in the PWS. Section F of the attached solicitation identifies the Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), service descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and performance periods. Quoters shall complete the price schedule with firm-fixed monthly MOS pricing for the base period and each option period. The Total Evaluated Price will include the base period and all three option periods. Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the best value to the Government. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability and Management Approach, Past Performance, and Price. When combined, the non-price factors are significantly more important than Price. The Government intends to make a selection from initial quotations but reserves the right to request clarification, additional information, or revised quotations when determined appropriate. Questions must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) Central Standard Time (CST) on November 20, 2026. Quotations must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) CST on November 30, 2026. Submit questions and quotations electronically to David.Jones@ihs.gov, referencing RFQ No. 75H70627Q00018 � Rosebud APP Services in the email subject line. Quoters must have a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), current System for Award Management (SAM) registration, and satisfy all applicable eligibility, responsibility, and exclusion requirements before award. Applicable solicitation provisions and contract clauses are identified in the attached Provisions and Clauses schedule. Prospective quoters are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation, PWS and addendum, price schedule, quotation instructions, evaluation criteria, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form, and any amendments before submitting a quotation.

If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. The Contractor must demonstrate technical capability conducting Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) bench-, pilot-, or full-scale efficacy evaluations targeting PFAS breakthrough and mass removal kinetics with preferred experience evaluating and optimizing existing pump-and-treat groundwater treatment plants (GWTPs) for PFAS removal across carbon be

title: NONSKID FOR NAVAL SHIPS/VESSELS
description: The award resulting from this RFP will be an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) supply contract with prepriced ELINS for Nonskid Deck Covering Removal/Replacement onboard U.S. Navy Ships. Nonskid replacement shall be accomplished meeting the following Society for Protective Coatings (SSPC) surface preparation standards: SSPC-SP10/National Association of Corrosion Engineers International (NACE) 2 Near-White Blast Cleaning SSPC-SP 11, Power Tool Cleaning to Bare Metal SSPC-SP12 WJ-3/NACE 5, Surface Preparation and Cleaning of Steel and other Hard Materials by High and Ultra High Pressure Water Jetting Prior to Recoating. Nonskid application will be either MIL-PRF-24667 Type I or Type V roll-on nonskid, Type IV spray on nonskid, or Type XI peel and stick sections.

title: ISBEE Solicitation: Emergency Department Registered Nurse Services (Up to 8 RNs) � Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates IHS Hospital, Fort Yates, ND.
description: The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for non-personal Emergency Department Registered Nurse services in support of the Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates Hospital, Fort Yates, North Dakota, under Solicitation No. 75H70627R00002. The requirement is for up to eight (8) qualified Emergency Department Registered Nurse positions to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day-per-week Emergency Department operations. The anticipated contract type is Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), commercial services, with one four (4)-month Base Period and fourteen (14) four-month Option Periods, for a total potential period of performance of sixty (60) months. This acquisition is set aside 100 percent for eligible Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) in accordance with the Buy Indian Act and applicable HHSAR requirements. The applicable NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, and the Product Service Code is Q401, Medical�Nursing. The Contractor will be responsible for providing qualified nursing personnel and all associated management, supervision, recruitment, credentialing, scheduling, replacement staffing, administrative support, and other resources necessary to perform the requirements of the Performance Work Statement. The requirement consists of up to eight (8) separately exercisable RN positions. The Base Period provides for up to eight (8) RN position CLINs, with the actual number of Base Period RN position CLINs awarded or funded identified in the resulting contract. During each Option Period, the Government may independently exercise from one (1) up to eight (8) RN position CLINs based on operational requirements and availability of funds. The Government is not obligated to award, fund, or exercise all eight RN positions, any particular RN position, or any Option Period. Pricing will be based on a common Firm-Fixed-Price RN Month of Service (RN/MOS) unit price for each performance period. The common RN/MOS unit price will apply uniformly to all RN positions within that performance period. The Total Evaluated Price will be based on the maximum potential requirement for the Base Period and all fourteen Option Periods; evaluation of all RN position CLINs and option prices does not obligate the Government to award, fund, or exercise all positions or options. Important Dates: Questions regarding the solicitation are due no later than November 13, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Proposals are due no later than November 30, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Award will be made using a Best Value Tradeoff process. Evaluation factors are Past Performance, Technical Approach, Management Approach, and Price. Past Performance, Technical Approach, and Management Approach, when combined, are more important than Price. Technical Approach and Management Approach will be evaluated using adjectival ratings of Outstanding, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable. The Government may select a higher-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits of the non-price factors justify the associated price premium. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement, Price Schedule/Bid Sheet, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, Buy Indian Act/ISBEE representations, wage determination, and any amendments, prior to submitting an offer.

description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested offerors should monitor PIEE and SAM.gov for any applicable solicitation amendments, thereafter. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to the attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Alicia Vesey, at alicia.m.vesey.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Paul Kang, at paul.k.kang.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR QUOTE, OR INVITATION FOR BID. The following are specialty qualifications necessary to perform this work: The Project Manager shall supervise a qualified crew of divers throughout the duration of this contract. title: Torque Calibration System Upgrade 250 ft-lbf
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program is considering a purchase of a Snap-on TTC400, or equivalent, torque transducer for calibrating snap action, dial, beam, and digital type torque wrenches, torque screwdrivers, and pneumatic/electric torque tools. AFMETCAL is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing a new torque transducer that will replace the Air Force's current 250 lbf-ft capability that is a part of the Snap-on TTC250LT-M Torque Calibration System. The provided equipment must be capable of covering torque values from 5 lbf-in to 250 lbf-ft, without gaps, and shall have an accuracy of �0.5% of Reading, or better. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity is 76 units over 5 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. description: Seeking information from interested Contractors for market research purposes regarding the availability and capability of Contractors to provide various compressed gases, cryogenic fluids, and related services for the Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base (HAFB), Utah.
